correctness.rationale: Poissonization of the discrete one-coordinate Bernoulli refresh chain makes coordinate update clocks independent rates w_i. Starting all zero, target probability q^m prod_i(1-e^{-w_i t}); starting all one, q^m prod_i(1+r e^{-w_i t}) with r=p/q. Strong Markov first-passage convolution at the all-one target implies exact Laplace-resolvent ratio, whose inclusion-exclusion expansion gives the claimed PGF for s=(1-z)/z. Both transforms have 1/s poles; the finite constant terms yield E N=Σ_{S!=∅}(r^|S|-(-1)^|S|)/w_S, including p=0. Independent m=3 nonuniform rational absorbing-chain solution at weights (1/2,1/3,1/6), p=2/5 yielded mean 919/54 matching direct subset sum. For fixed t, log(1+r e^{-w_i t}) is convex (constant if r=0), while log(1-e^{-w_i t}) is strictly concave for w_i>0; Karamata gives strict Schur-convexity of integrand and expected hitting time, so uniform unique minimizer. The geometric success-block lower bound proves finiteness for positive weights. This covers all finite m, positive weights, 0<=p<1; does not claim stochastic order of the law.

value.rationale: In a natural actively nonmonotone coupon collection system the sampling probabilities are controllable, and the theorem supplies the exact hitting-time transform and a strict all-parameter balancing optimum rather than an arbitrary small instance. It distinguishes genuine selected-coordinate erasure from monotone or global-reset collection.

limitations: Common refresh-success q>0, iid positive sample weights finite m; no adaptive/nonuniform loss per coordinate.
Schur-convexity proof applies to expectation, not all stochastic-order functionals.
